subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by a shared reply-session initialization fix, or by adding explicit retry/spool parity to each non-Telegram inbound surface?
rationale: The source and logs support a real message-loss bug, but the best fix layer changes session lifecycle semantics and overlaps with an open proof-positive PR whose scope may be permanent wedges rather than transient distinct-message drops.

options.title: Review shared boundary fix first
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 or an equivalent shared serialization fix as the primary path, then verify this issue's transient WebChat, heartbeat, and channel drops before closure.

options.title: Require surface retry parity
options.body: Keep the shared self-heal separate and require explicit retry or spool handling for WebChat, heartbeat, Signal, Discord, and any remaining unprotected inbound handlers.

options.title: Ask for focused live proof
options.body: Request one focused current-main live reproduction of the transient distinct-message path if maintainers need more proof before choosing the owner boundary.

recommendation.title: Review shared boundary fix first
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 or an equivalent shared serialization fix as the primary path, then verify this issue's transient WebChat, heartbeat, and channel drops before closure.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest recent history on the session-accessor boundary where a shared owner-boundary fix would likely land.
